heroText: I build .NET services across commerce, search, data and operations. My work connects API design with the consistency and reliability of the wider system.
demoLabel: Choose a domain. See its relationships and my work.
initialNode: Catalog, categories and variants connect the customer-facing API with search, cache and source data.
tryFailure: What happens on a cache miss?
workIntro: Three examples of decisions across service boundaries. Explore the problem, my contribution and the resulting behaviour.
searchNameOutcome: I redesigned a complex category and indexing flow in Elasticsearch.
searchProblem: Category mapping and index rebuilds had become difficult to maintain and could produce inconsistent results.
searchContribution: I identified the problems and redesigned the flow, owning the work from diagnosis through implementation and regression tests.
searchDecision: I treated category correctness and concurrent index updates as one design problem.
resultsearch: I corrected category and media mapping and added coordination for index rebuild requests.
searchCaseOpen: Read the story: redesigning category search
searchCaseOwnership: I took the initiative to rework a complex Elasticsearch flow, from investigating the problems to designing and implementing the solution.
searchCaseBefore: Category relationships, media mapping and overlapping index rebuilds were difficult to manage together.
searchCaseMapping: I reworked category mapping and removed repeated processing from the flow.
searchCaseHierarchy: I corrected parent-category media selection and handled circular category relationships.
searchCaseCoordination: I designed rebuild coordination to account for new requests arriving while an update is running.
searchCaseAfter: The reworked flow brings category mapping, media selection and index rebuild coordination into one design.
searchCaseTestHierarchy: Parent and child categories map to the expected hierarchy.
searchCaseTestMedia: Parent media comes from the actual parent category.
searchCaseTestCycle: Traversal does not revisit a category cycle.
searchContext: Search behaviour / Indexing workflows / Data consistency
caseProductNameOutcome: I redesigned manufacturer discovery and category counts to work together.
productProblem: Manufacturer lists and category counts could disagree as search filters changed.
productContribution: I traced the inconsistency and redesigned the discovery flow so the list and its category counts stay aligned.
productDecision: I addressed the query and cache behavior together, rather than patching the displayed counts.
identityNameOutcome: Role-aware administration and Excel exports delivered as a stream.
identityProblem: Administrative workflows join permissions, account data, reporting and large exports across services.
identityContribution: I developed dashboard counts, multiple-role handling, impersonation sessions, localised streaming Excel exports and product-request validation.
identityDecision: Make access boundaries explicit and avoid buffering an entire export when a stream can carry the result.
resultidentity: Administrative features include dashboard counts and multiple-role handling. Localised Excel export is streamed instead of assembling the complete file in memory.
dataNameOutcome: Redis pre-checks and more precise cache keys.
dataProblem: A cache entry, relational record and search document represent different versions of the same business fact.
dataContribution: I added Redis pre-checks to variant queries, refined manufacturer cache keys and invalidation after successful writes, and worked on targeted relational projections.
dataDecision: Keep the source of truth explicit. Invalidate after a successful write, and preserve query semantics while reducing unnecessary reads.
casePlatformNameOutcome: I designed shared event-handling behavior for .NET services.
platformProblem: Services needed consistent ways to handle events and failures across multiple operations.
platformContribution: In 2024, I designed shared MediatR infrastructure with selectable failure-handling policies. I also developed background media jobs and resolved scheduled-job issues.
platformDecision: I moved event-handling rules into shared infrastructure so each service could select the behavior it needed.
opsNameOutcome: Timing and traceability across service workflows.
opsProblem: A failed request may start in one service and become visible in another. Understanding the runtime matters as much as reading the code.
opsContribution: I diagnose service failures through Elasticsearch, application logs, background jobs and container state, working with delivery and operational tooling.
opsDecision: Use logs, timing and service state together to narrow down a failure before changing behaviour.
casePaymentNameOutcome: Provider integrations, refunds and reconciliation safeguards.
paymentProblem: Payment providers, order records and ERP documents can disagree after a timeout or a partial refund.
paymentContribution: I built payment provider integrations, cancellation and refund flows, event-driven state handling and checks around downstream accounting operations.
paymentDecision: Treat an uncertain provider result explicitly. Reconcile before repeating a financial operation.
paymentContext: Payment providers / Cancellation and refunds / ERP integration
experienceIntro: From enterprise commerce and industrial IoT to platform integrations. I work through service boundaries, data consistency and operational failures.
ozdisanWork: I develop product, search, identity, order and payment service flows. My work spans query projections, cache invalidation, event processing, back-office reporting and diagnosis across service boundaries.
icredibleWork: I developed .NET backend services and external API integrations for CMS and low-code workflows, working with PostgreSQL, Elasticsearch, Redis and Kafka.
fiverrContext: Independent software delivery through a freelance marketplace
fiverrWork: I built custom applications from requirements to API delivery, including asynchronous RabbitMQ workflows and database access.
kocWork: On Platform 360, I worked on asset management, identity and multi-tenancy. I developed features for IoT sensor data and real-time Modbus processing, and contributed to shared Carbon library maintenance and CI/CD.
poldyWork: I worked on technical support, reporting and integrations, translating operational needs into actionable technical work.
qnbWork: For Dijital Köprü’s C#.NET integration application, I developed and maintained SQL queries for data transfer with ERP systems. I diagnosed transfer failures and provided technical documentation and second-level support.
